calls.head: Tampa Bay hunts better looks than Minnesota
calls.body: Tampa Bay ranks 5th of 32 for shot quality, toward the point-blank end; Minnesota ranks 25th, toward the perimeter end.
calls.call: Tampa Bay’s shots are more dangerous on average than Minnesota’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average unblocked shot was, Tampa Bay had 1 goal per 17.1 shots and Minnesota 1 goal per 15.1 shots. Coming in, Tampa Bay was at 1 goal per 15.0 shots and Minnesota at 1 goal per 16.4 shots.
calls.usual: TBL 1 goal per 15.0 shots · MIN 1 goal per 16.4 shots
calls.tonight: TBL 1 goal per 17.1 shots · MIN 1 goal per 15.1 shots

calls.head: One stingy defense, one porous one
calls.body: Tampa Bay ranks 4th of 32 for shot suppression, toward the stingy end; Minnesota ranks 18th, toward the porous end.
calls.call: Tampa Bay allows fewer 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than Minnesota.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts allowed per 60, Tampa Bay had 55.4 per 60 and Minnesota 76.6 per 60. Coming in, Tampa Bay was at 51.2 per 60 and Minnesota at 57.3 per 60.

TBL.head: We had this close to even (57% for Tampa Bay), and Tampa Bay came through.

MIN.head: We had this close to even (43% for Minnesota), and it went Tampa Bay’s way.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Tampa Bay’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 48, against its usual 96 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Minnesota tried a different line
surprises.body: J. Eriksson Ek, K. Kaprizov, M. Boldy played 9:32 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Minnesota’s usual lines.
